compiled:
📰 General

League of Legends’ 2XKO Launch Faces Technical Issues on PlayStation 5 •

Riot Games’ free-to-play fighting game, 2XKO, launched yesterday across PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PlayStation 5 following an 18-month closed beta. Initial reports indicate the game is experiencing technical issues on the PS5 platform. Players are encountering problems with performance and stability during gameplay. Riot Games has yet to officially address the issues or provide a timeline for potential fixes. The game’s launch has been met with mixed reactions due to these technical difficulties.

🌍 World

Trump Criticizes Mark Carney’s Davos Remarks, Demands Canadian Gratitude •

During a speech at the World Economic Forum in Davos, former President Donald Trump directly addressed Prime Minister Mark Carney, accusing him of delivering a negative assessment of the United States. Trump argued that Carney’s remarks regarding the U.S. economy warranted a demonstration of gratitude from Canada. The former president’s comments followed Carney’s previous day’s address, which focused on concerns about the U.S.’s economic policies and their impact on global stability. Trump’s remarks were delivered amidst ongoing trade tensions between the two nations.

🦅 US

Nathan’s Famous Hot Dog Empire Sold to Smithfield Foods for $450 Million •

Nathan’s Famous, a Coney Island institution established over a century ago, has been acquired by Smithfield Foods in a significant all-cash transaction. The deal valued the iconic hot dog maker at $450 million, marking a major shift in the brand’s ownership. Smithfield Foods, a leading packaged meat company, will now control the operations and distribution of Nathan’s Famous products. The sale represents a substantial investment for Smithfield, solidifying its presence in the prepared foods market.

💰 Business

Supreme Court Grapples with Trump’s Challenge to Fed Governor Lisa Cook’s Appointment •

The Supreme Court heard arguments regarding Donald Trump’s request to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook, focusing on allegations of bias related to her past financial dealings. Justice Alito expressed concerns about the court’s role in resolving factual disputes within the Fed’s internal investigations. The court questioned whether Governor Cook received adequate notification of the accusations and a sufficient opportunity to respond. The justices indicated a reluctance to intervene prematurely in the ongoing investigation, suggesting the matter requires further factual determination.

💻 Technology

AMD Rolls Out New Adrenalin 26.1.1 WHQL Drivers for Enhanced Gaming Performance •

AMD has released a new Adrenalin Edition 26.1.1 WHQL driver update for its Radeon graphics cards. This update focuses on stability and performance improvements following rigorous testing by Microsoft's Windows Hardware Quality Labs (WHQL). The driver includes optimizations for various games and applications, aiming to address potential issues reported by users. Specifically, the update resolves reported application launch failures with non-English character usernames on Radeon RX 7000 and RX 9000 series cards. Users are advised to update to ensure optimal performance and stability.

🎭 Entertainment

Prue Leith Announces Departure From ‘The Great British Baking Show’ •

Prue Leith, a judge on “The Great British Baking Show,” has announced her decision to step down from the role. The announcement was made via an Instagram post, marking the end of her nine-series tenure on the popular baking competition. Leith cited judging over 400 challenges as the reason for her departure. The show’s producers have confirmed her exit, and a replacement judge has not yet been announced.

🏅 Sports

Alabama Basketball Star Charles Bediako Receives Immediate NCAA Eligibility After NBA Contract Dispute •

Charles Bediako, a prospective Alabama basketball player, has been granted immediate NCAA eligibility following a court ruling. A temporary restraining order issued by an Alabama judge allows Bediako to play for the University of Alabama despite previously signing contracts with NBA teams. The decision stems from a legal challenge to the NBA’s ability to restrict players from competing in college basketball. This ruling highlights a continuing conflict between the NBA and NCAA regarding player eligibility.

🔬 Science

Physicists Suggest Gravity Isn’t Fundamental, Tied to Universal Disorder •

A new theoretical framework proposes that gravity’s influence throughout the universe could be a consequence of entropy, rather than a fundamental force. Physicist Ginestra Bia developed this theory, suggesting that the observed gravitational effects are a manifestation of the universe’s inherent tendency towards disorder. The research posits that entropy, a measure of randomness, is the underlying mechanism driving the attraction between celestial bodies. This innovative approach could potentially unify our understanding of gravity with thermodynamics.

🩺 Health

Tiny Terrier Woody Undergoes Rare Brain Surgery, Now Recovering Well •

A six-year-old terrier mix named Woody underwent a complex and rare brain surgery at DoveLewis Animal Hospital in Portland, Oregon. Surgeons successfully removed a previously undetected tumor located in Woody’s skull. The tumor was identified through advanced imaging techniques and posed a significant threat to the dog’s neurological function. Following the successful operation, Woody is currently recovering and responding positively to treatment. Veterinary staff are optimistic about his continued recovery and long-term prognosis.
